compound.name: citral (geranial/neral)
compound.one_liner: The lemon aldehyde pair (geranial + neral) of lemon balm oil and lemon basils.

identity.note: CID 8843 is the double-bond-unspecified mixture record (geranial + neral). Component: PubChem CID 638011 (title 'Citral') is the (2E) isomer = geranial, IUPAC (2E)-3,7-dimethylocta-2,6-dienal, InChIKey WTEVQBCEXWBHNA-JXMROGBWSA-N, ChEBI CHEBI:16980 (read). Neral (Z) record could not be read (PubChem HTTP 503 on CID 643779) - null.

occurrences.source_citation: Majdi C, Pereira C, Dias MI, et al. (2020) Phytochemical characterization and bioactive properties of cinnamon basil (Ocimum basilicum cv. 'Cinnamon') and lemon basil (Ocimum × citriodorum). Antioxidants 9(5):369
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: TODO(author): cultivar-specific composition. The only paper value found is citral 4.9 % of volatiles in Ocimum × citriodorum (linalool 32.8 % dominant), not O. basilicum 'Mrs Burns' Lemon'. Duke's species-level O. basilicum records list citral up to 700000 ppm of oil. Duke (O. basilicum): CITRAL Essential Oil max 700000 ppm; Plant 560-7000 ppm; GERANIAL Leaf EO max 2000; NERAL Leaf EO max 1000 ppm. Paper value: citral 4.9 % of total volatiles in lemon basil, where linalool (32.8 %) was the major compound - but the paper's lemon basil is Ocimum × citriodorum, not O. basilicum s.str. (see flags). | Basis as recorded: ppm as listed by Duke (basis not stated per row; for 'Essent. Oil' parts it is ppm of the oil, 10000 ppm = 1 %)

occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: EMA: 'Essential oil 0.06-0.8% containing monoterpene aldehydes, mainly citral, neral and citronellal'; no per-component % given. Duke: GERANIAL Shoot 10-1425 ppm; NERAL Shoot 10-1100 ppm; CITRAL Shoot (no value, Hager). | Basis as recorded: essential oil content of the dried leaf (citral is a main constituent of the oil)

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Lemon balm yields only 0.06-0.8 % oil from dried leaf [8]. Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

compound.teaching_note: Lemon balm smells strongly of lemon yet yields very little oil (0.06-0.8 %), which is one reason its oil is costly and often adulterated [8]. For 'Mrs Burns' Lemon' basil the only value found was for O. × citriodorum, where citral was 4.9 % and linalool dominant [19].
gaps: PubChem CID 8843 is the geranial + neral mixture record; the neral (Z) record (CID 643779) could not be read.
Mrs Burns' Lemon: cultivar-specific composition and taxon (O. basilicum var. vs O. × citriodorum / O. × africanum) unresolved.
No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
